title: Dictionary: Feynman path integral $\leftrightarrow$ QOU categorical trace
html:
The correspondence between the Feynman path integral formalism and the QOU categorical trace is strict.

See Table.

Three finite computations of the path integral. The categorical trace admits three independent evaluation methods, each producing the same finite answer without regularisation:

  1. Multiplicative integral (analytic): \mathfrak{m} = \lVert\mathrm{MI}\int_\Sigma(\nabla_A q, L \wedge F^+)\rVert. The surface \Sigma is the disc swept by the photon threading the hadron braid. The multiplicative integral accumulates the connection along this surface.

  2. Ribbon trace (algebraic): \mathfrak{m} = \lVert\mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{ribbon}}(\rho(\beta))\rVert \cdot (q-1)^2. The Reshetikhin--Turaev invariant evaluated in the ribbon category gives the crossing energy. The factor (q-1)^2 = c_q^{-2} converts to mass.

  3. Gröbner--Shirshov reduction (computational): \mathfrak{m} = (q-1)^2 \sum |c_w| \cdot |q - q^{-1}|. Each Hecke step \sigma_i^2 \to (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1 contributes a discrete term. Yang--Baxter moves are free. Confluence ensures path independence (gauge invariance).

Photon threading as insertion of a complete set of states. The Feynman propagator inserts a complete set of intermediate states. The QOU analogue is photon threading. The photon strand \gamma passes through the hadron braid \beta_{\mathfrak{H}}, encountering each crossing sequentially. Each crossing contributes a Hecke step (eigenvalue insertion). The braid crossings act as intermediate states. The Hecke relation provides the eigenvalue decomposition at each insertion.
